patch.value: pm extension --init and pm package init are divergent scaffold generators behind the same grammar; the extension path emits no tests and an unpublishable manifest

Two scaffold generators are reachable through near-identical grammar and produce materially different quality. Verified against dist build 2026.7.25 by running both with identical arguments.

pm extension --init <path> --capability commands emits 5 files: index.ts, manifest.json, package.json, README.md, tsconfig.json. Its package.json is the single line {"type": "module"} with no name, version, license, scripts, engines, peerDependencies or pm block. There is no test file and no .gitignore.

pm package --init <path> --capability commands emits 7 files: the same five plus .gitignore and index.test.ts, and its package.json is a complete publishable manifest with name, version, keywords, engines, typecheck/test scripts, peerDependencies on @unbrained/pm-cli, devDependencies, and the full pm block (aliases, extensions, docs, examples, catalog with display_name/category/summary/tags). The generated manifests are byte-identical apart from the name, and index.ts differs.

Consequence for the stated goal of making package creation as easy as possible: an agent or author who reasons 'I am building an extension' reaches for the extension noun, which is also where --capability is documented in pm extension --help, and lands on the degraded generator. Its next_steps never mention that pm package init exists or that it produces the fuller starter, so nothing routes the author to the better path. docs/EXTENSIONS.md describes the rich behaviour (per-capability starters with a colocated node:test suite built on the SDK assertRegistered*/runRegistered*ForTest helpers) under the package noun, so the extension path silently diverges from its own documentation. The result is a starter with zero tests in a project that enforces 100% coverage internally and publishes a dedicated @unbrained/pm-cli/sdk/testing subpath, and a package.json that cannot be published or installed as a pm package without being hand-rewritten to the shape every real unbraind pm-* repository uses.

Related evidence for pm-quzx: the good generator itself mints an unbounded peer range, peerDependencies {"@unbrained/pm-cli": ">=2026.6.24"}, so the scaffold is an upstream source of the unbounded-range pattern that item already tracks.

The extension and package scaffold paths share one generator so identical arguments produce identical output, or the extension path is explicitly narrowed to a documented sub-case and its output and next_steps state which fuller path to use instead. Every scaffold path that produces an installable artifact emits a colocated test built on the public SDK testing helpers and a package.json that pm install accepts without hand editing. Documentation in docs/EXTENSIONS.md matches the behaviour of both nouns. A regression test asserts scaffold parity between the two entry points for every --capability value.
